summary: Filed a new child question (@legal_term_inbound) plus one focused experiment that closes the weakest joint in the main finding. Motivation: every receipt behind the MsgForgetLeader classification account delivered the peer-form message with no term field at all, and the parent rationale even explains the acceptance by saying the term-less wire form is treated as a local message — so the finding looked like it might collapse into the already-refuted term-zero path and depend on an illegal field. Source reading (raft.go:1096-1101 term switch, raft.go:1264-1268 default dispatch, raft.go:1749-1757 stepFollower case) says the term never gates the message: a non-zero term equal to the receiver's own matches no case and falls through to the default dispatch, which reaches stepFollower, which clears r.lead without reading the term. Two new source anchors were recorded for those branches. The new harness test (TestAssuranceForgetLeaderLegalTerm) delivers a real heartbeat (control: lead 1), the candidate's real pre-vote under the live lease (control: no grant), then the same MsgForgetLeader type with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 — a real voter and a well-formed term — and then the identical pre-vote again, with four comparisons covering both controls and both consequences. All ten TestAssurance functions compile and pass together in the scratch copy; the local smoke run emitted accepted=true, step_error="", lead 1 -> 0 for the well-formed message and granted=true for the pre-vote afterwards, so the classification gap appears to stand with no illegal field needed — but that judgment is left to the controller receipt, which is what will decide it either way. If the receipt holds, the parent rationale's causal clause about the unset term needs correcting and the finding is strengthened; if it is refused, the finding shrinks to the refuted term-zero path. Update validated: valid=true, execution_requested=true.
